result:
The api died because the disk filled up: a `report-export` job wrote about 20 GB to `/var/lib/stockroom` in eight minutes, the database ran out of space, and the api exited and never came back.

One thing to check first: every timestamp in `logs/service.log` is from 2026-03-09 (02:00–05:30), not last night. Either this is an old or sample log, or the clock on that host is wrong, so confirm this is the incident you mean.

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 03:05:00 | `report-export` starts writing 512 MB CSV parts to `/var/lib/stockroom/exports/`, one every 12 seconds |
| 03:09:03 | `WARN disk /var/lib/stockroom at 91%` |
| 03:12:48 | 40th and last export part written (about 20 GB total) |
| 03:13:30 | `WARN disk /var/lib/stockroom at 99%` |
| 03:14:00 | `ERROR db: could not extend file "base/16384/2619": No space left on device` |
| 03:14:03 | `ERROR api: transaction aborted, shutting down worker pool` |
| 03:14:06 | `FATAL api: exiting (status 1)` |
| 03:16:00 onward | `ERROR proxy: upstream api refused connection` every 2 minutes until the log ends at 05:29:57 |

- **No recovery:** there is not a single api line after 03:14:06, so it was still down when the log ends, over two hours later. `docker-compose.yml` sets `restart: unless-stopped` on the api, yet the log shows no restart or startup line of any kind.
- **Other services:** web and proxy kept serving 200s throughout; only the api was lost.
- **Cache warnings are unrelated:** the `cache: slow command` warnings (100–150 ms) occur at the same rate all night, before and after the crash.

The log does not show what started the export or why it produced so much. I did not trace the job to its code; `scripts/audit_export.py` is the only export-related file in `scripts/` or `app/` and is the place to look next.

To bring the api back, free space under `/var/lib/stockroom/exports/` first, since the database shares that volume and will fail again otherwise.
